programmes.d: A new lineup of celebrities joins the World Poker Tour for episode eight of the WPT Hollywood Home Game.
WPT Commentator Mike Sexton is joined by world famous poker pros Daniel Negreanu, Annie Duke and Phil Hellmuth.
Two of the Discovery Networks most popular shows face off for a night of exciting poker action on a special episode of the World Poker Tour.
Luck is a lady once again as the finest female players in poker are back to battle it out in Ladies Night II.
The WPT is back! Season three of the best poker on television kicks off in high gear with a high stakes duel in the Las Vegas desert.
There are fireworks on the Jersey shore as one of the most talent laden WPT final tables ever explodes with action at the $3,000,000 Borgata Poker Open.
He's back. The trash talking Tony G. has once again made the final table in Paris and the motor mouthed Australian hasn't mellowed with time.

The WPT tips its hat to the godfather of poker with the launch of the inaugural "Doyle Brunson North American Poker Championship" and a final table loaded with star power worthy of the master himself.
Surf's up as the World Poker Tour heads back to Aruba where fun in the sun means poker on the beach and one lucky player's vacation ends with a million dollar payday.

Six and a half million dollars. Even the world's largest casino is barely big enough to contain this final table as the enormous Foxwoods Resort and Casino becomes ground zero for one of the largest poker tournaments in history.
Sin City rings up a heavenly payout as Bellagio in Las Vegas hosts the final table of the five million dollar Five Diamond World Poker Classic.
Cinderella gets a tan as the WPT soaks up the fun in the Bahamas with a table full of reckless newcomers and a scorching $3,500,000 prize pool.
In Mississippi it's an epic David vs. Goliath battle as three young guns go up against three of the biggest names in poker for a river of cash – over $5,000,000.
Southern California is rockin' and rollin' as the WPT shakes up Los Angeles with the largest prize pool in west coast history.
